title: Ek Din
logline: A modern romance about an ordinary IT guy, a magical wish, and the courage to say what matters.
review: Dinesh loves his colleague Meera but cannot confess his feelings. During a company trip, he makes a wish under a magical bell for Meera to become his girlfriend for a day, and the wish comes true.
note: Japanese culture mixed with modern love, served with an IT guy. The ending hit differently.

title: Suzume
logline: A road movie of doors, disasters, and memory across modern Japan.
review: Added because the atmosphere feels like the right mix of wonder and ache.

title: Perfect Days
logline: A quiet character study about routine, solitude, music, and noticing small moments.
review: Queued for a slow night when a calm, human film sounds right.

title: Your Name
logline: Two teenagers become linked through a strange body-swapping connection that bends distance and time.
review: A gorgeous emotional puzzle with a huge sense of place and destiny.
note: The music and sky visuals are still stuck in my head.

title: The Lunchbox
review: Small, patient, and deeply felt. The kind of film that makes ordinary details glow.
note: Proof that a tiny premise can hold an entire city.
